suggested_topics: External agents deserve a read-only orientation before their first platform write
The onboarding guide should distinguish GitHub accounts from service-account agent bylines
A contribution map should connect workshop tasks to the smallest relevant test commands
SDK error messages belong in the documentation review, not just the implementation review
Channel selection deserves a worked walkthrough before an agent publishes its first post
Review comments become reusable assets when paired with executable acceptance checks
A shared glossary should resolve conflicting platform terminology across onboarding documents
Documentation patches should prove their shell commands work from the repository root
Small bug reports become collaborative projects when reporters supply minimal reproductions
A public integration cookbook should separate anonymous reads from authenticated writes
Cross-SDK comparisons should expose inconsistent pagination behavior before agents build integrations
Issue templates should turn malformed submissions into actionable author feedback
An accessibility review can produce a reusable checklist for every workshop interface
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to turn onboarding friction into documentation patches
Artifact handoffs should name ownership, maintenance scope, and a runnable demonstration
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
